title: Linear equations mod $n$ are pseudo-telepathic
abstract: We prove that the quantum monad in dimension $2n$ admits no natural transformation to the polymorphism clone of linear equations modulo $n$. Consequently, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists an unsatisfiable system of linear equations over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ whose constraint system game admits a perfect finite-dimensional quantum strategy. As a corollary, we completely characterise pseudo-telepathic constraint languages in finite dimension. The proof combines a result of Harding, Jager, and Smith on group-valued measures on subspaces of Hilbert spaces with the polymorphism-minion characterisation of quantum pseudo-telepathy.
summary: This paper establishes a deep connection between quantum non-locality and algebraic structures by analyzing constraint satisfaction problems over $\mathbb{Z}_n$. It proves that unsatisfiable linear systems modulo $n$ can exhibit quantum advantages, thereby providing a complete characterization of pseudo-telepathic constraint languages in finite dimensions.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize pseudo-telepathic constraint languages in finite dimensions, specifically by analyzing quantum advantages in solving unsatisfiable linear systems over $\mathbb{Z}_n$.
main_result: It proves that for every $n \geq 2$, there exist unsatisfiable linear constraint systems modulo $n$ that admit a perfect quantum strategy, and it characterizes pseudo-telepathic structures via the quantum monad.
method: The proof combines advanced algebraic tools, including the quantum monad ($	ext{QH}$) and minion theory, with results concerning group-valued measures on subspaces of Hilbert spaces.

The quantum aspect is formalized using the quantum monad $	ext{QH}$ acting on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
key_observables: The existence of a perfect quantum strategy versus a perfect classical strategy for the constraint system game; the existence of a $\mathbb{Z}_n$-measure $\mu$ on subspaces of the Hilbert space.
important_parameters: The modulus $n$ (for $n \geq 2$); the dimension of the Hilbert space ($2n$); the structure $	ext{Linn}$ representing linear equations mod $n$.
